page: Vultr vhp-1c-2gb-intel is a virtual private server within the High Performance family, configured with 1 shared vCPU and 2.0 GB of system memory. Powered by an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor operating at 2.0 GHz, this single-core, single-threaded instance includes 50 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and one complimentary public IPv4 address. The CPU architecture supports instruction sets such as AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI for vector neural network instructions, AES cryptography, and BMI2.

Benchmark evaluations place this instance in the lower performance tiers. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests both scored 1357.59, reflecting the shared nature of its single physical core. Memory bandwidth is constrained, with large-block read and write speeds measuring 5.68 GB/sec and 4.43 GB/sec respectively, which falls into the bottom 10% of tested systems. Database and key-value store performance are similarly limited, with Redis SET operations executing at 1.61 million operations per second and Passmark database operations scoring 467.55.

The primary tradeoff of this server is its shared CPU allocation and low memory capacity, which restrict its capability under sustained or multi-threaded workloads. However, the inclusion of local NVMe SSD storage provides fast disk I/O relative to standard block storage. From a cost-efficiency perspective, this hardware profile represents a low-cost entry point for basic hosting needs where high computational density or dedicated CPU resources are not required.

This server is suitable for lightweight, non-critical workloads. Appropriate use cases include static web serving, basic application prototyping, small-scale development environments, simple cron jobs, or running lightweight utility services that do not demand high memory or continuous CPU utilization.
